species.real: Bannau Brycheiniog, the Brecon Beacons in Wales, take their English name from the signal fires once lit on high ground there.
species.name: Beaconet

dex.text: A little iron fire-basket with a flame for a head, found on hilltops after dark. Sees a long way, and tells everybody what it saw.
dex.fact: Beacons on high ground were kept ready to be lit in 1588, to pass the warning of the Spanish Armada quickly from the coast inland.

species.real: The old chain was lit again for fun in 1988, four hundred years after the Armada, and royal jubilees still bring the beacons out across the country.
species.name: Beaconblaze

dex.text: Stands on the headland in the teeth of the gale and burns all the brighter for it. When one lights up, the next one along the coast lights too, and the next, until the whole country knows.
dex.fact: Plymouth Hoe and Haldon Hill were among the beacon sites of Devon; a fire seen from one hilltop could be answered by the next within minutes.
